description: CUSTFILE OPEN, a keyed READ that hits, then the CLOSE that reports '00' - the three CALLs app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL makes around one customer lookup, pinned end to end. Dispatch. EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD at app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:118 selects WHEN 'CUSTFILE' at :123 and performs 3000-CUSTFILE-PROC THRU 3999-EXIT at :124. That arm is the THIRD of the four, so every call here proves the ordered dispatch runs past 'TRNXFILE' (:119) and 'XREFFILE' (:121) before it matches (gate G30), and LK-M03B-DD is pinned on all three images so the claim is checked rather than assumed. The guarded paragraph. 3000-CUSTFILE-PROC (:181-204) is three sequential IF ... END-IF blocks and not one of them carries an ELSE: IF M03B-OPEN at :183 does OPEN INPUT CUST-FILE at :184 then GO TO 3900-EXIT at :185; IF M03B-READ-K at :188 does MOVE LK-M03B-KEY (1:LK-M03B-KEY-LN) TO FD-CUST-ID and READ CUST-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT at :189-190 then GO TO 3900-EXIT at :192; IF M03B-CLOSE at :195 does CLOSE CUST-FILE at :196 then GO TO 3900-EXIT at :197. Because no ELSE exists, reaching the CLOSE proves the two earlier guards were both evaluated and both failed, and preserving that order is what gate G30 and rule R7 ask of restructured control flow - the third image below is where it becomes observable. All three paths converge on 3900-EXIT (:200-201), whose single statement is MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC, and then on 3999-EXIT (:203-204). Every LK-M03B-RC of '00' below is therefore that one MOVE, reading the CUSTFILE-STATUS area declared at :91-93 - the THIRD of four independent two-byte status areas (:83-97), none of which carries a VALUE clause, which is why a status is asserted per DD and never globally (gate G47). CUSTFILE is ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM (:45), so this paragraph guards M03B-OPEN, M03B-READ-K and M03B-CLOSE and has no IF M03B-READ at all, unlike the two SEQUENTIAL DDs. The caller idiom transcribed. Call one is 8300-CUSTFILE-OPEN (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:783-799): MOVE 'CUSTFILE' TO WS-M03B-DD, SET M03B-OPEN TO TRUE, MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC, CALL 'CBSTM03B' USING WS-M03B-AREA. Call two is 2000-CUSTFILE-GET (:368-390), which sets M03B-READ-K (:371), moves XREF-CUST-ID into the key (:372), zeroes and then COMPUTEs WS-M03B-KEY-LN = LENGTH OF XREF-CUST-ID (:373-374) so the length is nine, and clears the record area with MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT (:376) before calling. Call three is 9300-CUSTFILE-CLOSE (:889-903), which resets the status with MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC (:892) but does NOT reset WS-M03B-FLDT; that is why the CLOSE image still carries the customer record the keyed read delivered rather than spaces, and reproducing that residue is part of what is pinned here. What a status means is decided by the caller, and the three callers are deliberately asymmetric: the OPEN at :789 and the CLOSE at :895 both accept '00' OR '04' - a wider tolerance than anything the read allows - while the keyed read at :379-386 accepts only '00' and sends everything else to WHEN OTHER, DISPLAY 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. Keeping that decision there is the parity requirement. Return code and messages. expectedReturnCode is 0 because CBSTM03B contains no RETURN-CODE reference anywhere and simply GOBACKs at :130-131; LK-M03B-RC is a FILE STATUS, not the return code, and the two are deliberately not conflated. expectedMessages is empty because the subroutine contains no DISPLAY statement at all - 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTFILE' at CBSTM03A.CBL:898 belongs to the caller. Widths, re-derivable by hand (practice B11). Each area image is 1040 bytes because LK-M03B-AREA (:100-112) is 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000, and all six spans are named individually on every image, so the whole 1040 is asserted field by field and not only as one string (gate G17). LK-M03B-KEY-LN is PIC S9(4) with no USAGE clause, so it is four zoned DISPLAY bytes with the sign overpunched into the low-order one: nine renders as '000I' and zero as '000{', and neither trailing character is a stray. READ ... INTO LK-M03B-FLDT at :190 is a group move of a 500-byte record into a 1000-byte receiver, so the record occupies the first 500 bytes and the remaining 500 stay spaces. Each customer row is 500 bytes because app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy is 9+25+25+25+50+50+50+2+3+10+15+15+9+20+10+10+1+3+168, the last of those being the trailing FILLER - named explicitly in every final-state row below, which is the field-level proof that the span was emitted, since a record missing it would be short by exactly 168 (gates G19 and G21). The record and its copybook. The row decodes through app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy (statement.model.Stm03CustomerRecord) and never through app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy: CBSTM03A copies CUSTREC at :55 and moves LK-M03B-FLDT into that CUSTOMER-RECORD at :388. The two layouts are byte-identical and differ in exactly one field name, so the date pinned by name below is CUST-DOB-YYYYMMDD and not CVCUS01Y's CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD; they are kept apart precisely so field-for-field diffing stays meaningful, and using the other name would itself be a difference. Key 000000011 names the middle of the three seeded customers, so a keyed read that quietly returned the first row - the failure a single-row seed could never catch - is reported here. Read-only, proved twice. All four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph in CBSTM03B writes, so the three seeded rows must come back exactly as they went in. That is asserted row by row in expectedFinalState, every field named, and again at dataset level in expectedDatasets, where CUSTFILE is pinned at three rows of 500 bytes on the FINAL_STATE channel - a count and a width no row expectation can state on its own. No normalisation applies. The seeded rows are a full 500 bytes with CUSTREC's trailing FILLER X(168) already space-filled on disk, so nothing is padded here; the two recorded width normalisations are cardxref 36->50, which supplies CVACT03Y's trailing FILLER X(14) (gate G16, risk R-F), and USRSEC 57->80, and neither concerns this DD. Where one does apply, the pad belongs to the seeding side that owns it and never to a case file. Code page, named and never inferred (practice B8). Every byte above is US-ASCII, the code page of the authoritative fixtures under app/data/ASCII; IBM037 belongs to the reference-only EBCDIC datasets under app/data/EBCDIC and is deliberately not used here. It matters for the two bytes in this case that are neither digit nor space: the '{' of a zero key length and the 'I' of nine are 0x7B and 0x49 in US-ASCII and would be different bytes entirely under an EBCDIC reading. Two operation codes stay dark (practice B5). M03B-WRITE 'W' and M03B-REWRITE 'Z' are declared at :107-108 and are never SET anywhere in app/cbl, so this case drives neither; they remain declared and unexercised rather than invented into life. The unit (gate G12, requirement I3, practice B4). The prompt-mandated Java name is StatementGenerationJobB, but CBSTM03B is not a job: its own header at :7 reads 'BATCH COBOL Subroutine', no EXEC PGM=CBSTM03B appears in app/jcl, app/proc or app/csd, and CBSTM03A CALLs it thirteen times. It is therefore a Spring @Component and unitKind is COMPONENT; the name divergence is recorded here rather than quietly corrected. The component is driven directly through its typed method, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). Role in the folder. case11 pins the keyed READ that misses with '23', case12 that miss followed by the plain READ which reaches no IF at all, and case20 interleaves CUSTFILE with the other three DDs; this is the one case of the twenty in which a CUSTFILE keyed READ succeeds and the file is then closed. Taken with the TRNXFILE CLOSE in case03, the XREFFILE CLOSEs in case07 and case08 and the ACCTFILE CLOSE in case13, the CLOSE operation is exercised on all four DD names across the folder, which is what gate G48 asks of the operation surface. Provenance (practice B12). Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - from the line numbers cited here, from the CUSTREC field offsets 0, 9, 34, 59, 84, 134, 184, 234, 236, 239, 249, 264, 279, 288, 308, 318, 328, 329 and 332, and from the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt rows 9 to 11 - and was NEVER captured from a COBOL execution. None runs in this environment: AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers, among them a COBOL compiler whose indexed file handler is disabled, which is exactly what an ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED file such as CUST-FILE (:43-47) would need, and the literal TAB characters in app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy, which break parsing outright. The deviation is one of provenance only - twenty cases per program, field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand unchanged - and it is escalated as risk R-A in AAP section 0.9.11.
